prompt:
The index proof is back on the desk before the volume is plated, so the editor lays the marked-up slip beside the page and photographs the pair.

The proof page carries three columns, each headed by one radical printed large, and the slip fixes the order the columns run in: the water radical 氵 first, then the hand radical 扌, then the tree radical 木. Under each head the characters filed there are set one to a line, a small figure printed to the right of each. The slip lists the characters this page has to take: 汁, 泳, 材, 案, 扮, 扣. The rule printed at the foot of the slip is that a character is filed under its own radical, that the figure beside it counts what is left once that radical is taken away, and that a column runs in the order of those figures.

Which column each character has gone into, and what figure stands beside it, the slip does not settle.
easy_question: Does this picture show a printed dictionary page with columns of Chinese characters set under large heading characters, and a marked-up slip of paper lying beside the page? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Read the small figures printed beside the characters down the middle column, from the top of that column to the bottom. Answer with one of: the figures get larger as you go down the column; the figures get smaller as you go down the column; the figures run up and down with no settled order.

Find the character 案 on the proof page. Answer with one of: it is standing in the left-hand column; it is standing in the middle column; it is standing in the right-hand column; it is standing outside the three columns.
